description:
Repro (base binary):
    def tag(x), do: x
    def main(), do: Enum.each([false, 0], fn v -> dbg(if(v, do: v, else: tag(:a))) end)
interp prints :a then 0. run prints :a, then panics at runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:286:10: fz_ref_load_atom ExpectedTag{expected: ValueKind(15), found: ValueKind(13)}. A literal :a in the else works, and so does a list of one type. With four mixed values a second panic appeared: "cannot coerce atom and numeric raw ABI reprs". Done when: an Elixir-oracle fixture of this shape agrees on interp, run and build.
title: The JIT reads an if's value correctly when its else calls a function over a list of false and 0
